Add group membership from what filers report on Form 990 line H

Source: R/md-ingest-efile-group.R
md_ingest_efile_group.Rd

The 990 header carries three group fields that md_ingest_efile_header() reads past: H(a) RETURN_GROUP_X (is this a group return), H(b) ALL_AFFIL_INCL_X (are all subordinates included) and H(c) GROUP_EXEMPT_NUM. H(c) is the organisation's own statement of the group it belongs to, filed annually, and it is a different witness from the BMF.

Usage

md_ingest_efile_group(con = NULL, dir = NULL, version = "v2_2")

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

dir

Directory of F9-P00-T00-HEADER-*.CSV.

version

Pinned efile_header version; also names dir when it is NULL.

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

What it adds that the BMF cannot

Measured over 2009-2024, 259,368 filings carry a usable GEN across 42,997 EINs and 3,497 groups. Against the pinned BMF:


  (EIN, GEN) pairs in the e-file        43,603
    BMF records no GEN for that EIN      7,015
    BMF agrees                          34,806
    BMF disagrees                        1,782

The 7,015 are the point. They are organisations that told the IRS on their own return which group they belong to and whose BMF row does not say so - more than twice what the NCCS historical extract contributed.

The second thing it adds is time. The BMF is a snapshot with no notion of when membership began or ended; a filing is dated. New rows therefore carry first_year/last_year from the tax years the claim was actually filed in, and n_obs counts the filings asserting it.

Disagreements resolve to the BMF, on vintage

The 1,782 conflicts are settled the same way md_ingest_group_meta() settles its 1,219: the BMF is a 2026-07 snapshot and the e-file runs to 2024, so the newer source wins. As there, the rule is enforced by construction - rows are only written for EINs the BMF gives no GEN at all - so a conflict cannot overwrite anything. The count is reported rather than absorbed.

The 34,806 agreements are deliberately not written. They would duplicate edges md_ingest_relations() already emitted, to say the same thing twice. The cost is that those edges stay untimestamped; timestamping an edge owned by another source is a cross-source update and does not belong in an append-only ingest. Left for a compile-time join if a consumer ever needs it.

Placeholder GENs are not group exemption numbers

0000 (1,352 filings), 0001 (1,291) and 9999 (315) are what filers put in the box when they have nothing to put in the box. They are dropped. So is anything that does not reduce to four digits.

Finding the parent, and admitting when it cannot be found

Membership is stored parent-to-member (§4: never a clique), so every group needs a parent. Three sources are tried in order, most authoritative first:

  1. the BMF's own coded parent - affiliation_code 6 or 8, per md_ingest_relations(). Covers 2,504 of the 3,497 groups.

  2. an EIN that filed a group return under that GEN. A group return is filed by the central organisation, so H(a) plus H(c) is a parent claim. Covers 96 more.

  3. gen_parent, the derived GEN-to-parent table. Covers 37 more. No ingest builds it (it was made by hand in the first database), so it is used only when the table exists, and a build from scratch skips it.

860 groups (25%) still have no identifiable parent and produce no rows. That is reported, not patched: inventing a parent to make the join succeed would fabricate the hierarchy the table exists to record.
